title: Write a three-line note in Mousepad and save it under a given name

capabilities.why: Mousepad, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

setup.why: Open Mousepad on a new, untitled document.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && exec mousepad

setup.why: Wait for Mousepad's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, and put the pointer on it: with no window manager, keys go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class mousepad | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Mousepad window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); sleep 1

instruction: In Mousepad, write a note with these three lines, in this order, one per line: "{{note.l1}}", "{{note.l2}}", "{{note.l3}}". Save it as {{note.name}}-{{nonce}}.txt in the folder /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}. This desktop has no window manager: keys go to the window under the mouse pointer.

checks.why: The saved file holds exactly the three lines in order (leading and trailing blank space aside). After setup the folder is empty, so an agent that does nothing fails.

teardown.why: Close Mousepad without saving (KILL: Mousepad holds on to a changed document on TERM) and delete the run's folder.

oracle.why: Type the three lines, then Save (Ctrl+S) opens the save dialog centred over Mousepad, under the pointer, with its name field selected: type the whole path there, pause for the field's completion, and press Enter.
